trust.role: LinkedIn RS256 ID-token verifier, not a user-info bearer access token. Published supported claim profile omits nonce, so token is reusable until expiry; account still binds the submitted Aztec transaction nonce/action.
trust.rotationRevocation: Refresh only the fixed provider JWKS endpoint. Review kid/SPKI rotation and explicitly update enrolled account policy; this snapshot is not a perpetual trust guarantee.
trust.authentication: Fetched from the configured official HTTPS JWKS URL with redirect errors; host trust store validates TLS; no token-selected jku/x5u resolution. JWKS provenance proves only public-key origin, not an issuer-signed user credential.

verification.method: Parse the official public JWKS and compute stable SPKI fingerprints. This does not verify a user token.

provenance.generator: packages/credential-proofs-inputs/tests/linkedin.test.ts generates a local 4096-bit RSA key and signs synthetic tokens; repository example fixture is also synthetic.

trust.role: Public repository synthetic token fixture only. It is not Facebook/LinkedIn-issued evidence and cannot establish successful real-provider sign-in.
trust.rotationRevocation: No production use; recreate or replace only with an explicitly documented local test fixture.
trust.authentication: Fixture is signed with a test-only local key or test-generated ephemeral key. Never enroll the test key as a production issuer key.

verification.method: Run the exact synthetic example witness and focused constrained claim-policy tests. No provider-test credential is supplied.
verification.verifier: nargo 1.0.0-rc.3 and local synthetic credential tests

acquisitionNotes.reason: No publicly reusable provider-issued test ID-token sample was captured. An authentic JWKS snapshot establishes public key provenance only; local examples and tests use synthetic keys/tokens. Live client registration and genuine login interoperability are not claimed.
